description: The session counter at its top, as ESP-IDF's security2.c handles it, after the handshake of srpCase (key is the first 32 bytes of its session key; sessionId the board's 8 bytes from response 1's nonce). The harness sets the board's counter to startCounter (security2.c's own session state; it takes 4 billion messages to get there otherwise) and the phone's to the same. Each message gives its counter, nonce, plaintext and sealed bytes; refused means the board refused that write. security2.c steps the counter after every message, wrapping from 0xffffffff to 0, and refuses to open or seal at 0; a request at 0xffffffff is opened and acted on but its answer cannot be sealed. So a phone seals no request at 0xffffffff, and the last answer it can receive is at 0xffffffff.
source: ESP-IDF v6.1.1 (commit 051e4c4eb20346e043cdd47bc388fde75ff8af63): components/protocomm/src/security/security2.c, src/common/protocomm.c, src/crypto/srp6a/esp_srp.c and esp_srp_mpi.c, proto-c/*.pb-c.c; protobuf-c 1.4.1 (commit abc67a11c6db271bedbb9f58be85d6f4e2ea8389); Mbed TLS 4.1.1 with TF-PSA-Crypto (commit ce3f3485a121c100f58f36d700cb35b060f6e866). Compiled for the host and run by packages/protocol/src/pairing/esp-idf/make-vectors.sh

cases.name: from 0xfffffffd: a request at fffffffd and its answer at fffffffe; the next request, at ffffffff, is opened and acted on by the board, which then cannot seal its answer and refuses the write
from 0xfffffffe: a request at fffffffe and its answer at ffffffff; the counter is then 0, and a request sealed at 0 is refused before it is opened
